DILG BAGONG PIUP'NAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, west Triangle, Quezon City www.dilq.qov.ph OPINION NO. MAY 20 2025 RONNIE S. ACUNA Acting City Vice Mayor Office of the Sangguniang Panlungsod of Marikina Marikina City Hall, Shoe Ave., Brgy. Sta. Elena Marikina City THRU: Ms. JANET S. OBISPO Human Resource Management Officer Dear Acting Vice Mayor Acuna: This has reference to the letter dated April 14, 2025, from Ms. Obispo, forwarding your 10 April 2025 letter, seeking guidance regarding the designation of thirteen (13) acting members of the Sangguniang Panlungsod (SP) of Marikina by this Department. Specifically, you seek clarification on two issues: I. Whether the individuals designated, absent formal appointments, are entitled to the salary attached to the positions to which they were designated, in light of DILG Legal Opinion No. 19, s. 2019, and the rulings in Dimaandal v. Commission on Audit and COA Decision No. 95-087 dated 02 February 1995; and 2. Whether said designees may be granted Representation and Transportation Allowance (RATA) in view of the provisions of COMELEC Resolution No. 11059, particularly Rule Ill, Section 8 in relation to Rule I, Section I(e). We address the first issue as follows: Upon review, we find that the circumstances of the present case are not analogous to those in DILG Legal Opinion No. 19, s. 2019. The said Opinion addressed internal designation under a different factual context, whereas the current matter involves the external designation of individuals to temporarily perform legislative functions due to the preventive suspension of all incumbent members of the Sanggunian. Given this distinction, we find said legal opinion inapplicable. "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

Nonetheless, this Department is of the considered view that the designated individuals may be entitled to receive the salary corresponding to the positions they presently occupy in a de facto capacity. Jurisprudence recognizes the doctrine of the de facto officer, which applies to a person who performs the duties of a public office under color of title in good faith, albeit without a legally valid appointment. In Menzon v. Petilla, the Supreme Court held that: "Under the principle of public policy on which the de facto officer doctrine is based, and on basic considerations of justice, it would be iniquitous to deny a de facto officer the salary for services he has actually rendered." Thus, in line with established jurisprudence and equitable considerations, we find no legal impediment to the payment of salaries to the designated SP members who are discharging official functions in good faith and in the exigency of public service. As to the second issue, we answer in the affirmative. Rule I, Section 1 (e) of the afore- cited COMELEC Resolution reads: "Giving of remuneration or privilege shall include giving of bonuses, other than the mandated 13th month pay and cash gift for government employees, incentives, representation and transportation allowance (RATA) or other form of allowances regularly received, on top of their usual benefits and privileges." (Emphasis supplied) Meanwhile, Section 8, Rule III of the same Resolution provides: "Total Ban on Promotion, Salary Increases, Grant of Privileges — The promotion or giving of increase of salary or remuneration or privilege to any government official or employee including those in GOCCs, shall be strictly prohibited from March 28, 2025 (Friday) until May 11, 2025 (Sunday)." Notably, the phrase "other than the mandated 13th month pay and cash gift" serves as an explicit exception to the coverage of the election ban. While RATA is included in the enumeration of privileges, the same provision clarifies that the prohibition pertains to increases in remuneration or privilege, not their continued grant if such were already regularly received. Accordingly, we are of the view that the COMELEC Resolution does not bar the continued receipt of RATA by the designated SP members, provided that such allowance is inherently attached to the position and not an additional or newly granted benefit during the prohibited period, This opinion is rendered based solely on the facts and representations contained in your correspondence and our appreciation thereof. It is without prejudice to any contrary determination by the Commission on Audit, the Commission on Elections, or competent judicial authorities. Page 2 of 3

We hope to have been of assistance. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: ATTY. ROMEO P. BENITEZ Undersecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSELLNRPB/LLLS-LRALLD/jam page 3 of 3
